headline: Coastal Louisiana Beach and Wetland Access
reservation: Grand Isle State Park handles campsite and pier access; verify status via the Louisiana State Parks portal. While the island beaches are public, specific glamping sites or private fishing charters require independent booking. Always check official sources for changing coastal access rules and seasonal park closures.

days.title: Bayou Gateway and Barrier Island Arrival

stops.name: Highway 1 Wetlands
stops.detail: Observe the transition from cypress swamps to salt marshes as you cross the elevated bridges toward the coast.

stops.name: Grand Isle State Park
stops.detail: Visit the observation tower for a 360-degree view of the Gulf of Mexico and the Caminada Pass.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours; conditions vary by weather and bridge openings
days.note: Check for local bridge maintenance schedules on the way south.

days.title: Coastal Heritage and Migratory Birding
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Grand Isle Beach

stops.name: Grand Isle Birding Trail
stops.detail: Walk through protected oak 'cheniers' to see migratory species sheltered in the ancient coastal forest.

stops.name: Island Fishing Pier
stops.detail: Cast a line or observe local anglers targeting trout and drum from this extended Gulf structure.

days.driving: Local walking or short island transfers; allow for sandy conditions
days.note: Bird sightings peak in spring and fall; insect activity varies with the breeze.

days.title: Gulf Exploration and Local Markets

stops.name: Back Bay Marshes
stops.detail: Explore the calm leeward waters by kayak to spot dolphins and marsh birds.

stops.name: Island Seafood Markets
stops.detail: Visit local vendors to learn about the seasonal shrimp and oyster harvest.

days.driving: Minimal driving; primarily local island routes
days.note: Tide levels can significantly impact marsh navigation and pier access.

intel.title: Beach and Park Staging
intel.text: State Park parking is concentrated at the east end; public beach access points are scattered along the main road. Soft sand can impede non-4WD vehicles if you leave paved areas.

intel.title: Coastal Connectivity
intel.text: Signal is generally reliable in the town center but can drop significantly in the outlying marsh areas. Download maps before leaving the Golden Meadow gateway.

intel.title: Island Supply Points
intel.text: Fuel is available on the island, but availability can be affected by regional storm events. It is standard practice to top off in Golden Meadow or Larose.

intel.title: Seasonal Shifts
intel.text: Spring and fall offer the most temperate weather for outdoor activities. Summer humidity is high, and winter can be damp and windy.

intel.title: Barrier Island Transit
intel.text: Access depends entirely on Highway 1; check for road flooding during high tides or tropical systems. The island is small enough for bicycles but requires a vehicle for the trip from the mainland.

plan.arrival: Pick up rentals at MSY, then secure supplies in Houma or Golden Meadow before the final stretch over the marsh. Check-in logic favors arriving before dusk to navigate the island roads.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for the highway; check rental contracts for restrictions on driving in sandy or coastal areas. Large RVs are common but require confirmed site lengths at the state park.
plan.goldenHour: The State Park Pier provides a Gulf-facing view for sunset, though seasonal clouds frequently shift the light.
